- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.20) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp spikes or drops.
- After a price spike, model often overcorrects and forecasts a sharp decline — suppress this overcorrection by smoothing the drop.
- Mean reversion bias: model overuses recent high prices as anchor, ignoring sentiment-driven volatility.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model still forecasts upward — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — sentiment shifts over 3–5 days can invalidate short-term trends.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often misses the rebound — add a 1–2 day lagged sentiment multiplier to forecast.
